questions.stem: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. Angle A = 85 degrees and angle B = 102 degrees. What is angle C?
questions.explanation: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180 degrees. Angle C = 180 - angle A = 180 - 85 = 95 degrees.

questions.stem: A tangent touches a circle at point T. The centre is O and OT = 5 cm. A line from O meets the tangent at point P, where OP = 13 cm. What is the length TP?
questions.explanation: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at T, so triangle OTP is right-angled at T. By Pythagoras: TP = sqrt(13^2 - 5^2) = sqrt(169 - 25) = sqrt(144) = 12 cm.

questions.stem: Two tangents from an external point P touch a circle of radius 4 cm at points A and B. The distance from P to the centre O is 8 cm. What is angle APB?
questions.explanation: In right triangle OAP: sin(angle APO) = OA/OP = 4/8 = 1/2, so angle APO = 30 degrees. Since PO bisects angle APB: angle APB = 2 x 30 = 60 degrees.

questions.stem: A tangent at point T on a circle makes an angle of 65 degrees with chord TC. Point D is on the major arc TC. What is angle TDC?
questions.explanation: By the alternate segment theorem, the angle between the tangent and chord TC equals the angle in the alternate segment. So angle TDC = 65 degrees.

questions.stem: In a circle with centre O, a tangent at A makes an angle of 50 degrees with chord AB. C is a point on the circumference on the other side of AB from the tangent. What is angle AOB?
questions.explanation: By the alternate segment theorem, angle ACB = 50 degrees. By the angle at the centre theorem, angle AOB = 2 x angle ACB = 2 x 50 = 100 degrees.
